question: Why does the will of the Lord contradict the doctrine of a single moment?
premises: Momentariness treats reality as a single passing moment.
The Lord's will governs continuity and order.
This governance conflicts with strict momentariness.
inference: The Lord's will opposes the doctrine of isolated momentary existence.
plain_english: It is not so that there is only one moment; that view is contradicted by the will of the Lord.
